boundaries.evidence: Statement/proof: The statement is immediate for the zero distribution; its transforms and inverse-error pairings vanish.
Statement/proof: The statement excludes zero frequencies and zero leading amplitude; positive radial frequency is treated explicitly in the final proof step.
Statement/proof: The statement and each displayed norm/composition formula include n=1; multi-index sums reduce to one-dimensional sums and the same radius split works.
Statement/proof: The statement requires a positive quadratic phase margin and nonzero leading amplitude. Without ellipticity the inverse is not asserted.

Statement/proof: The statement uses lambda>=1. Optimal truncation estimates are for large lambda; bounded lambda are included by increasing the finite constant. Parameter neighborhoods are shrunk compactly before their constants are chosen.
Statement/proof: The proof uses unique formal inverses, uniquely selected local critical points, finite truncations and finite covers. No arbitrary-index selection or new choice assumption is used.
Statement/proof: The reconstruction representation transfers exponential estimates in the statement from a source elliptic packet family to any target family.
Statement/proof: The proof interchanges the two elliptic packet families and constructs the reverse representation, giving both implications in the statement.
Statement/proof: If the support is empty, the distribution and every Gaussian transform vanish, so the statement holds.
Statement/proof: Zero input is covered directly; the normal covectors in the statement are nonzero. The proof is valid for complex distributions without reality symmetry.
Statement/proof: For n=1 the tangential variable zprime is absent; the proof becomes exactly the single complex-normal-variable rectangle and Gaussian approximate-identity argument.
Statement/proof: The flat hypersurface has nonzero normal by its coordinate definition; there is no degenerate-normal case in the statement.

Statement/proof: The rectangle barrier is zero on three boundary sides and between zero and one on its left side, where the boundary estimates are proved. Both frequency orientations are propagated through the same connected left half-plane.

Statement/proof: The proof uses a finite explicit disk chain on a bounded polygonal path and a fixed analytic harmonic barrier. Its distributional approximate identity uses uniform continuity and Gaussian tails, not sequential selection.
Statement/proof: One absent oriented normal forces local vanishing by the proof, as the statement asserts.
Statement/proof: The equivalent support-point assertion in the statement follows by contraposition separately for both normal orientations; local vanishing makes every local packet pairing zero.
Statement/proof: The statement holds immediately for empty support, since u=0 and Ru=0.
Statement/proof: The statement excludes the zero data covector. Zero object covectors cannot occur in the nonzero incidence relation because both projections are submersions.
Statement/proof: A finite cover consisting of one chart uses rho_1,N=chi_1,N; the partition and integration-by-parts estimates in the proof still hold.

Statement/proof: The proof derives a uniform nonzero fiber phase derivative from the empty cotangent fiber. Degenerate/stationary pieces are not assumed nonstationary; they are excluded by the hypothesis.
Statement/proof: Every integration-by-parts localizer is compact in its chart, so all integration boundary terms vanish. Data-cutoff transitions are handled instead by a positive Gaussian separation.
Statement/proof: The proof uses a finite compact cover and an explicit product partition, avoiding uncontrolled reciprocals of cutoff sums and arbitrary choice.
Statement/proof: This is a one-way statement; its forward implication is proved by the fixed-order transpose estimate.
Statement/proof: No converse is claimed in the statement: nonzero stationary contributions may cancel, so regularity is not asserted to imply an empty relation fiber.
Statement/proof: The statement holds for u=0 by zero pairings and exact linearity.
Statement/proof: The relation point in the statement has nonzero object and data covectors. The positive real radial normalization does not introduce zero covectors.

Statement/proof: The Gaussian wavepacket normalization and regularization in the proof are valid in one dimension as algebraic identities; the double-fibration dimension assumptions themselves still apply to every admitted incidence.

Statement/proof: The proof derives strict reduced imaginary Hessian positivity from injectivity of d pi_L; a zero reduced direction would yield a forbidden tangent kernel. Vanishing amplitude is excluded by the corrected transform definition.

Statement/proof: The proof keeps the contour boundary fixed with a positive imaginary margin and estimates each fixed derivative of its exponential error before distributional pairing. Bounded frequency parameters are handled by compact neighborhoods.

Statement/proof: The analytic section selects a finite invertible minor; critical points are locally unique. Exact packet resolution is proved using Gaussian frequency regularization, avoiding the countable-choice hypothesis of the existing Fourier-inversion supplier.
Statement/proof: The one-way regularity implication in the statement follows by the analytic section and general elliptic packet criterion.
Statement/proof: No reverse operator regularity implication is asserted in the statement; only the local object recovery implication is proved.

finite_checks.calculation: Htt=2+i, Htx=3, Hxx=5+i, tau=-3/(2+i)=(-6+3i)/5. Reduced Hxx-Hxt Htt^-1 Htx=(7+14i)/5. |T Re(tau)+D|^2+|T Im(tau)|^2=36/25+1+9/25=14/5. The imaginary parts match and are positive.
